---
title: Config repo
guide-section: Get Started
---

Your settings live in a private repo you own, apart from the code. Start from the template:

1. Open [ha-automations-config-template](https://github.com/joshwlivingston/ha-automations-config-template) and select **Use this template > Create a new repository**.
2. Make it **private**, since `apps.yaml` contains entity IDs.

The template has:

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `apps.yaml` | your app instances, with an example for each app to edit |
| `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` | deploys to your Home Assistant box, see [Deploy](deploy.qmd) |

Its README is a step-by-step setup guide.

## apps.yaml

Each top-level key is one app instance. The key is the app's name, and `module` and `class` say which app it is:

```yaml
bedroom_sunrise:
  module: sunrise_fade
  class: SunriseFade
  light: light.bedroom_lamp

living_room_sunset:
  module: sunset_fade
  class: SunsetFade
  light: light.living_room_lamp
  max_brightness: 30
```

| app | module | class |
|---|---|---|
| [Sunrise Fade](../docs/apps/sunrise-fade.qmd) | `sunrise_fade` | `SunriseFade` |
| [Sunset Fade](../docs/apps/sunset-fade.qmd) | `sunset_fade` | `SunsetFade` |
| [Light Fade](../docs/apps/light-fade.qmd) | `light_fade` | `LightFadeApp` |

Every other key is a setting for that app. Each app page lists its settings. Unknown settings are an error, so a typo shows up in the AppDaemon log instead of being ignored.

The app name also names its test event: `bedroom_sunrise` listens for `bedroom_sunrise_start`.

## Deploy settings

The deploy workflow needs to know where your Home Assistant box is and which repo to install from. See [Deploy](deploy.qmd).
